explanation: 1. Head start: in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), Maya covers 8 × 1/4 = 2 miles. 2. Rosa gains 18 − 8 = 10 miles per hour. 3. Time to close the gap: 2 ÷ 10 = 1/5 hour = 12 minutes.

question: Luis is saving for a new bike. He puts $3 in a jar the first week, and every week after that he puts in $1 more than the week before. He started the plan on his 15th birthday. How much will Luis have saved in all after 9 weeks?
explanation: 1. Week 9: $3 + 8 × $1 = $11. 2. Pair week 1 with week 9, week 2 with week 8, and so on: each pair adds to $3 + $11 = $14. 3. With 9 weeks, the average week is $14 ÷ 2 = $7, so the total is 9 × $7 = $63.

question: Yuki is laying square pavers for a backyard patio. The patio will be a rectangle 12 feet by 10 feet, and each paver is 12 inches on a side. The pavers fit exactly, with no cutting. How many pavers does Yuki need?
explanation: 1. 12 inches is 1 foot, so each paver covers 1 square foot. 2. Area: 12 × 10 = 120 square feet, so 120 pavers.

question: Luis is making lasagna for 8 guests and wants it ready to serve at 7:00 p.m. sharp. Assembling it takes 25 minutes, baking takes 55 minutes, and it must rest 15 minutes before serving. These steps happen one after another. It is 5:15 p.m. now. At most, how many minutes can Luis wait before starting?
explanation: 1. Time needed: 25 + 55 + 15 = 95 minutes. 2. From 5:15 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. is 105 minutes. 3. Luis can wait 105 − 95 = 10 minutes.

question: Isaac ordered lunch from a café for a team meeting that ran 90 minutes. The order was four sandwich boxes at $15 each plus a fruit tray for $14. Sales tax is 6%, and he added a 20% tip figured on the food cost before tax. What was the total cost of the lunch order, including tax and tip?

Dmitri buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $40, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $44. He rides the bus about 16 days a month. By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
explanation: 1. Change in price: $44 − $40 = $4. 2. Compare it with the original price: $4 ÷ $40 = 1/10 = 0.1. 3. As a percent, that is an increase of 10%.

question: June's running club timed its members in a 5-kilometer race. The 15 runners in the morning group averaged 31 minutes, and the 10 runners in the evening group averaged 36 minutes. The course had four water stations. What was the average time for all the runners in both groups, in minutes?
explanation: 1. First group total: 15 × 31 = 465 minutes. 2. Second group total: 10 × 36 = 360 minutes. 3. Together: 465 + 360 = 825 minutes for 15 + 10 = 25 runners. 4. Average: 825 ÷ 25 = 33 minutes.

question: Jade is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes. How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
table: Option | Monthly fee | Cost per class / Membership | $50 | $14 / Drop-in | $0 | $19
explanation: 1. Membership costs $50 more up front. 2. Drop-in costs $5 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $5. 3. The gap closes after $50 ÷ $5 = 10 classes. 4. Check: $50 + 10 × $14 = $190 and $0 + 10 × $19 = $190, so the answer is 10 classes.

question: Caleb keeps a tin of cookies on his desk. It holds 3 chocolate chip cookies and 5 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from his neighbor 6 years ago. Without looking, he takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back. What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?
explanation: 1. There are 3 + 5 = 8 cookies in all. 2. P(both chocolate chip) = 3/8 × 2/7 = 6/56. 3. P(both oatmeal) = 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56. 4. Add the two cases: 6/56 + 20/56 = 26/56 = 13/28.

question: Theo spends a rainy Saturday watching a baking show. He watches three episodes, and each one is 30 minutes long. How many hours of the show does Theo watch?
explanation: 1. Total: 3 × 30 = 90 minutes. 2. There are 60 minutes in an hour: 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours.

question: Omar is driving to a lake house, which is 105 miles from home, and then driving back. His car gets 35 miles per gallon, and gas costs $4.10 per gallon. His car's tank holds 16 gallons. How much will gas cost for the round trip?
explanation: 1. Round trip: 2 × 105 = 210 miles. 2. Gas needed: 210 ÷ 35 = 6 gallons. 3. Cost: 6 × $4.10 = $24.60.

question: Paige is painting the four walls of her home office, which is 18 feet long, 8 feet wide and 9 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $42 a gallon. If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Paige need to buy?
explanation: 1. Wall area: 2 × (18 + 8) × 9 = 468 square feet. 2. Two coats: 468 × 2 = 936 square feet. 3. 936 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.7, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

question: Ruth's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes. What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
table: Goals scored | Number of games / 0 | 4 / 1 | 1 / 2 | 4 / 3 | 4 / 4 | 7 / 5 | 3
explanation: 1. Total: 4 + 1 + 4 + 4 + 7 + 3 = 23 games. 2. With 23 values in order, the median is the 12th value. 3. Running totals: through 0: 4, through 1: 5, through 2: 9, through 3: 13, through 4: 20, through 5: 23. 4. The 12th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

question: A café asked 120 regular customers which drinks they had ordered in the past month. The results are in the table. The "Iced coffee" and "Hot tea" counts include the customers who ordered both drinks. The café has 11 tables. How many customers ordered both drinks?
table: Answer | Number of customers / Iced coffee | 54 / Hot tea | 44 / Neither drink | 42
explanation: 1. At least one: 120 − 42 = 78. 2. Adding 54 + 44 = 98 counts the 'both' group twice. 3. So the extra count is the 'both' group: 98 − 78 = 20.

question: Priya is reading a 390-page novel for her book club and has already read 150 pages. She plans to read 30 pages each day until she finishes. How many more days will it take to finish the book?

Dmitri bowls in a league with 15 teams. So far this season he has bowled four games, scoring 170, 184, 187, and 148. He wants his average after the next game to be exactly 170. What score does Dmitri need in the next game?
explanation: 1. An average of 170 over 5 games means a total of 170 × 5 = 850. 2. Total so far: 170 + 184 + 187 + 148 = 689. 3. Needed: 850 − 689 = 161.

question: Esme wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $1,157 if she pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $100 down, then 6 monthly payments of $187. The couch is 90 inches long. How much more would Esme pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?
explanation: 1. Monthly payments: 6 × $187 = $1,122. 2. Payment plan total: $100 + $1,122 = $1,222. 3. Extra cost: $1,222 − $1,157 = $65.

question: Ava is growing bacteria for a biology lab. She starts a dish with 200 bacteria, and under these conditions the population doubles every 15 minutes. The dish is 10 centimeters across. How many bacteria will be in the dish after 1.5 hours?
explanation: 1. 1.5 hours = 90 minutes, which is 90 ÷ 15 = 6 doublings. 2. Double six times: 200 → 400 → 800 → 1,600 → 3,200 → 6,400 → 12,800 bacteria.

question: On level ground, Carmen holds a 3-foot yardstick straight up, and its shadow is 6 feet long. At the same moment, the shadow of a nearby oak tree is 31 feet long. The tree was planted about 53 years ago. How tall is the oak tree, in feet?
explanation: 1. The sun hits both at the same angle, so height ÷ shadow is the same for the oak tree and the yardstick: 3 ÷ 6. 2. Height of the oak tree = 31 × 3 ÷ 6 = 93 ÷ 6 = 15.5 feet.

question: Maya has been waiting for a sale on a rolling suitcase that normally costs $146. This weekend the store has it marked 50% off. What is the sale price of the rolling suitcase, before tax?

Theo bikes to work. He rides 3 miles on a bike path at a steady 12 miles per hour, then 4 miles through city streets at a steady 8 miles per hour. The bike path has 15 benches along the way. How many minutes does the whole trip take?
explanation: 1. First part: 3 ÷ 12 = 1/4 hour, which is 15 minutes. 2. Second part: 4 ÷ 8 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes. 3. Total: 15 + 30 = 45 minutes.

question: Carmen's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and her average so far. There are 32 students in the class, and only the final exam is left. What score does Carmen need on the final exam to finish with exactly an 85?
table: Category | Weight | Average / Homework | 20% | 84 / Quizzes | 30% | 92 / Midterm | 20% | 83 / Final exam | 30% | ?
explanation: 1. Points earned so far: 16.8 + 27.6 + 16.6 = 61. 2. To finish at 85, the final must add 85 − 61 = 24 points. 3. The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 24 ÷ 0.3 = 80.

question: Tariq is building a wooden garden gate shaped like a rectangle, 32 inches wide and 60 inches tall. To keep it from sagging, he will nail a straight brace from one corner to the opposite corner. The gate will hang on three hinges. How long must the brace be, in inches?
explanation: 1. The brace is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs equal to the width and height. 2. Shrink the numbers first: 32 = 4 × 8 and 60 = 4 × 15. 3. 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17², so the brace is 4 × 17 = 68 inches.

question: Caleb is organizing a kickball league with 8 teams this season. Every team will play every other team exactly twice during the regular season. Each game takes about 50 minutes. How many games will be played in the regular season?
explanation: 1. Each game is a pair of teams. Each of the 8 teams pairs with 7 others: 8 × 7 = 56. 2. That counts every pair twice, so divide by 2: 56 ÷ 2 = 28 pairs. 3. Each pair plays twice: 28 × 2 = 56 games.

question: Owen and four friends go bowling. The lanes cost $68 for the night, and shoe rentals add $24. They split the total evenly. How much does each person pay?
explanation: 1. Total: $68 + $24 = $92. 2. Owen plus four others makes 5 people. 3. Each pays $92 ÷ 5 = $18.40.

question: On a trip to Mexico, Leah exchanges money at a rate of 20 pesos per U.S. dollar. At an outdoor market, she buys a painted bowl for 650 pesos and a straw hat for 340 pesos. She has six days left on the trip. How much did Leah spend in all, in U.S. dollars?
explanation: 1. Total: 650 + 340 = 990 pesos. 2. Each dollar is 20 pesos: 990 ÷ 20 = $49.50.

question: Mei's club ran a bake sale on Saturday morning. They sold cookies, brownies and muffins in the ratio 6:5:1, and they sold 72 items in all. Every item was priced at $2.50. How many cookies did the club sell?
explanation: 1. Total parts: 6 + 5 + 1 = 12. 2. Each part is 72 ÷ 12 = 6 items. 3. Cookies: 6 parts × 6 = 36 cookies.

question: June owns 6 shares of a company's stock. On Monday the share price rose 10%. On Tuesday it fell 10% from Monday's closing price. By what percent is Tuesday's closing price lower than the price before Monday's change?
explanation: 1. Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way). 2. Up 10%: 100 → 110. 3. Then down 10%: 10% of 110 is 11, so 110 → 99. 4. 99 is 1 below 100, so it is 1% lower.

question: Dmitri is five times as old as his nephew, Eli. They live 14 blocks apart and walk together most weekends. Exactly 4 years ago, Dmitri was nine times as old as Eli. How old is Eli now, in years?
explanation: 1. Let Eli's age now be x, so Dmitri is 5x. 2. 4 years ago: 5x − 4 = 9(x − 4) = 9x − 36. 3. Move the x terms to one side: 4x = 36 − 4 = 32, so x = 8. 4. So Eli is 8 years old now. Check: 4 years ago, 36 = 9 × 4.

question: Fatima runs to the pet store for her dog. She buys a bag of treats for $6.25, a chew toy for $4.25, and a new leash for $11.50. There's no sales tax, and she pays with a $50 bill. How much change should Fatima get back?

A store is taking 50% off every winter coat, and Omar finds one with a regular price of $200. He also has a member coupon that takes 20% off the already reduced price. The sale price is good for 9 more days. How much does Omar pay for the winter coat, before tax?
explanation: 1. 50% of $200 is $100, so the sale price is $200 − $100 = $100. 2. The extra 20% comes off $100, not the original price: 20% of $100 is $20. 3. Final price: $100 − $20 = $80.

question: Wes bought a used car for $10,000. His mechanic estimates that the car will lose 20% of its value each year, based on what it is worth at the start of that year. The car gets about 29 miles per gallon. Using that estimate, what will the car be worth after 2 years?

Priya and Aiyana are painting the fence around their community garden. Working alone, Priya could paint it in 6 hours, and Aiyana could paint it in 24 hours. The fence is 150 feet long. If they work together, each at a steady pace, how many hours will the fence take?
explanation: 1. In one hour, Priya does 1/6 of the fence and Aiyana does 1/24. 2. Together: 1/6 + 1/24 = 4/24 + 1/24 = 5/24 of the fence per hour. 3. Time: 1 ÷ 5/24 = 24/5 = 4.8 hours.

question: The clock at the train station has a face 3 feet across. While Chloe waits on the platform, it reads 3:11. As on any ordinary clock, the hour hand moves steadily from one number toward the next as the minutes pass. What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
explanation: 1. The minute hand moves 6 degrees per minute: 11 × 6 = 66 degrees past the 12. 2. The hour hand is 30 degrees per hour plus 0.5 degree per minute: 3 × 30 + 11 × 0.5 = 95.5 degrees past the 12. 3. The gap between them: 95.5 − 66 = 29.5 degrees. 4. That's not more than 180, so the smaller angle is 29.5 degrees.

question: After a long hike, Sam stops at a cafe for dinner. His bill is $46.40 before tip. He always tips 15% of the bill. How much is the tip?

Mateo is planning a hike with a trail map where 1 centimeter represents 2 kilometers. The trail to the waterfall measures 4.5 centimeters on the map, and the trail back to the parking lot measures 6.5 centimeters. The parking lot has 30 spaces. How many kilometers long is the whole hike?
explanation: 1. Map distance: 4.5 + 6.5 = 11 centimeters. 2. Each centimeter is 2 kilometers: 11 × 2 = 22 kilometers.

question: Leah's company asked its employees how they usually get to work. Each person gave one answer, shown in the table. The office parking lot has 75 spaces. What percent of the employees surveyed chose either "Drive" or "Bus or train"?
table: Answer | Number of employees / Drive | 24 / Bus or train | 150 / Bike | 30 / Walk | 36

question: Fatima paddled a kayak 9 miles upstream at 2 miles per hour, then turned around and paddled the same 9 miles back downstream at 6 miles per hour. Her kayak is 10 feet long. What was Fatima's average speed for the whole round trip, in miles per hour?
explanation: 1. Upstream: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 hours. Downstream: 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5 hours. 2. Total: 18 miles in 4.5 + 1.5 = 6 hours. 3. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 miles per hour (not the simple average of the two speeds).

question: Grace empties the cup holder in her car and finds nothing but quarters and dimes. There are 18 coins in all, worth $2.85 together. She has had the car for 4 years. How many quarters are in the cup holder?
explanation: 1. Suppose all 18 were dimes: 18 × 10 cents = 180 cents. 2. The real total is 285 cents, which is 285 cents − 180 cents = 105 cents more. 3. Each quarter adds 15 cents more than a dime, so there are 105 cents ÷ 15 cents = 7 quarters (check: 7 × 15 cents = 105 cents).

question: The bell in the town hall tower rings once for each hour, with the rings evenly spaced. Amara times it at 7 o'clock: 24 seconds pass from the first ring to the last. How many seconds does it take from the first ring to the last at 11 o'clock?
explanation: 1. 7 rings have only 6 gaps between them, so each gap is 24 ÷ 6 = 4 seconds. 2. 11 rings have 10 gaps: 10 × 4 = 40 seconds.

question: Theo is building a rectangular pen for his chickens that measures 17 feet by 7 feet. He'll fence all four sides. How many feet of fencing does Theo need?
explanation: 1. One length plus one width: 17 + 7 = 24 feet. 2. Going all the way around doubles that: 2 × 24 = 48 feet.

question: Hugo works at a restaurant for $20 an hour. Any hours over 40 in a week are overtime, paid at 1.5 times his regular rate. The restaurant has 39 employees. Last week he worked six shifts of 8 hours each. How much did Hugo earn last week, before taxes?
explanation: 1. Hours worked: 6 × 8 = 48. 2. Regular pay: 40 × $20 = $800. 3. Overtime rate: 1.5 × $20 = $30 an hour, for 48 − 40 = 8 hours. 4. Overtime pay: 8 × $30 = $240. 5. Total: $800 + $240 = $1,040.

question: The water trough at Noor's farm is a rectangular metal tank 5 feet long, 2.5 feet wide and 2 feet deep. It serves the five horses in the north pasture. One cubic foot holds about 7.5 gallons of water. Using 7.5 gallons per cubic foot, how many gallons of water does the trough hold when completely full?
explanation: 1. Volume: 5 × 2.5 × 2 = 25 cubic feet. 2. Gallons: 25 × 7.5 = 187.5.

question: Ruth buys a monthly bus pass. Last year the pass cost $110, and this year the transit agency raised the price to $143. She rides the bus about 16 days a month. By what percent did the price of the bus pass increase?
explanation: 1. Change in price: $143 − $110 = $33. 2. Compare it with the original price: $33 ÷ $110 = 3/10 = 0.3. 3. As a percent, that is an increase of 30%.

question: Rosa mixed 3 liters of liquid plant food that is 30% concentrate. The label says seedlings need a mix that is only 15% concentrate, so she will dilute it with water. She is growing five trays of seedlings. How many liters of water should Rosa add?
explanation: 1. Concentrate now: 30% of 3 = 0.9 liters. 2. Adding water doesn't change that amount, so for it to be only 15% of the mix, the total must grow by a factor of 30/15 = 2: 3 × 2 = 6 liters. 3. Water to add: 6 − 3 = 3 liters.

question: Nadia is signing up for pottery classes at a local studio, which offers the two options in the table. Each class lasts 90 minutes. How many classes in a month would make the two options cost exactly the same?
table: Option | Monthly fee | Cost per class / Membership | $40 | $8 / Drop-in | $0 | $18
explanation: 1. Membership costs $40 more up front. 2. Drop-in costs $10 more per class, so each class closes the gap by $10. 3. The gap closes after $40 ÷ $10 = 4 classes. 4. Check: $40 + 4 × $8 = $72 and $0 + 4 × $18 = $72, so the answer is 4 classes.

question: Kofi, Kenji, Raul and two of their cousins are lining up in one row for a family photo. Kofi, Kenji and Raul are triplets and want to stand together, side by side. The photographer charges $60 for the session. In how many different orders can the 5 of them line up?
explanation: 1. Glue the three into one block, leaving 3 units: 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 orders. 2. Inside the block the three can be ordered 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways. 3. Total: 6 × 6 = 36.

question: Luis is shopping for a new bike helmet and finds one priced at $34. The sales tax where he lives is 5%, added at the register. What is the total cost of the bike helmet, including tax?

Theo is picking up donuts for the class's 8 a.m. study session. The donut shop sells donuts in packs of 4 for $3.50, or one at a time for $1.10 each. Fifteen students signed up, and Theo wants at least one donut per person. Leftovers are fine, but he can't split a pack. What is the least Theo can spend?
explanation: 1. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 full packs, with 3 people left over. 2. Option 1: 3 packs + 3 singles = $10.50 + $3.30 = $13.80. 3. Option 2: 4 packs = $14, with 1 extra. 4. The cheaper option is $13.80.

question: Jordan helped run a pancake breakfast at the fire station. Adult plates cost $9 and kids' plates cost $4. They served 230 plates and took in $1,315, with six volunteers working the griddles. How many adult plates did they serve?
explanation: 1. If all 230 were kids' plates, the total would be 230 × $4 = $920. 2. The actual total is $1,315 − $920 = $395 more than that. 3. Each adult plate brings in $5 more than each kids' plate, so adult plates: $395 ÷ $5 = 79.

question: Ben's living room has a round rug that is 8 feet across. He wants to replace it with a round rug that is 10 feet across. The room is 16 feet long. The new rug will cover how many times as much floor area as the old rug?
explanation: 1. Radii: 4 and 5 feet. 2. Areas: π × 4² = 16π and π × 5² = 25π. 3. Ratio: 25π ÷ 16π = 25/16.

question: Marcus and Hana start at opposite ends of a 6.5-mile lakeside path and walk toward each other. Marcus walks at 2 miles per hour, and Hana walks at 4 miles per hour. They leave at the same time. The lake is about 7 feet deep in the middle. How many minutes after they leave do they meet?
explanation: 1. The gap closes at 2 + 4 = 6 miles per hour. 2. Time to close 6.5 miles: 6.5 ÷ 6 = 13/12 hours. 3. 13/12 × 60 = 65 minutes.

question: A snail at the bottom of a 13-foot well climbs 3 feet up the wall every day, then slides back 2 feet every night while it rests. On which day does the snail first reach the top of the well, if the first day of climbing is day 1?
explanation: 1. Each full day and night, the snail gains 3 − 2 = 1 foot. 2. On its last day it climbs 3 feet and never slides back, so it only needs to start that day at 13 − 3 = 10 feet. 3. Reaching 10 feet takes 10 ÷ 1 = 10 full days and nights. 4. It reaches the top on day 10 + 1 = 11.

question: A farm stand sells a 3-pound bag of apples for $3.75. Ruth wants 10 pounds for pies, and the stand will weigh out any amount at the same price per pound. How much will 10 pounds of apples cost?

Priya is putting laminate flooring in a rectangular guest room that measures 15 feet by 11 feet. Each box of flooring covers 24 square feet and weighs 28 pounds. The store sells only whole boxes. Ignoring waste, how many boxes does Priya need to buy?
explanation: 1. Area: 15 × 11 = 165 square feet. 2. 6 boxes cover 6 × 24 = 144 square feet, which is not enough. 3. 7 boxes cover 168 square feet, so Priya needs 7 boxes.

question: Ava is stocking up on peanut butter and compares the three jar sizes in the table. She goes through about three jars a month. What is the difference, in cents, between the highest and lowest price per ounce among the three sizes?
table: Size | Amount | Price / Small | 24 oz | $3.12 / Medium | 32 oz | $3.52 / Large | 40 oz | $8.00
explanation: 1. Small: $3.12 ÷ 24 = 13¢ per ounce. 2. Medium: $3.52 ÷ 32 = 11¢ per ounce. 3. Large: $8.00 ÷ 40 = 20¢ per ounce. 4. Highest minus lowest: 20¢ − 11¢ = 9 cents.

question: At the warehouse where Kenji works, the 24 workers on the day shift packed an average of 45 boxes each on Monday. The 16 workers on the night shift, which started at 10 p.m., packed an average of 85 boxes each. What was the average number of boxes packed per worker across both shifts?
explanation: 1. First group total: 24 × 45 = 1,080 boxes. 2. Second group total: 16 × 85 = 1,360 boxes. 3. Together: 1,080 + 1,360 = 2,440 boxes for 24 + 16 = 40 workers. 4. Average: 2,440 ÷ 40 = 61 boxes.

question: Zoe's booth at the town festival has 10 rubber ducks floating in a pool. A player pays $5, picks one duck at random, and wins the prize marked underneath; the duck then goes back in. The table shows the prizes. The festival lasts 7 hours. On average, how much money does the booth make per game after paying out prizes?
table: Prize | Ducks / $10 | 1 / $1 | 4 / Nothing | 5
explanation: 1. If each duck came up once, the prizes would total 1 × $10 + 4 × $1 = $14. 2. Average prize per game: $14 ÷ 10 = $1.40. 3. The booth keeps $5 − $1.40 = $3.60 per game on average.

question: Jamal rode his bike to work four days this week. The rides took 27, 28, 31, and 34 minutes. What was his average ride time, in minutes?

Jade is stocking up at a garden center for her spring planting. The prices, with tax included, are in the table. The garden center is 3 miles from her house. Jade orders three bags of potting soil, one flower pot, and three watering cans. What is the total cost of Jade's order?
table: Item | Price / Bag of potting soil | $6.25 / Flower pot | $5.50 / Seed packet | $1.80 / Watering can | $8.99

question: Ava bought a pair of running shoes at a sporting-goods store during a 50%-off sale, and she also used a $15 coupon. The register took 50% off the original price first, then subtracted the coupon. Only four pairs in her size were left on the shelf. Before tax, Ava paid $56. What was the original price of the shoes?
explanation: 1. Add the coupon back: $56 + $15 = $71. 2. $71 is what was left after 50% off, so it is 50% of the original price. 3. Original price: $71 ÷ 0.5 = $142.

question: Sofia started walking along a straight lakeside path at a steady 3 miles per hour. Malik started running from the same spot 12 minutes later, going the same direction at a steady 6 miles per hour. The path is 6 miles long. How many minutes after starting to run did Malik catch up to Sofia?
explanation: 1. Head start: in 12 minutes (1/5 hour), Sofia covers 3 × 1/5 = 0.6 miles. 2. Malik gains 6 − 3 = 3 miles per hour. 3. Time to close the gap: 0.6 ÷ 3 = 1/5 hour = 12 minutes.

question: In a board game, Elena's piece is stuck in the jail space. Under the house rules, she rolls a standard six-sided die three times, and she escapes if any roll is a 6. The board has 30 spaces in all. What is the probability, as a fraction, that Elena escapes?
explanation: 1. Work with the opposite: one roll is not a 6 with probability 5/6. 2. No 6 in 3 rolls: (5/6)³ = 125/216. 3. At least one 6: 1 − 125/216 = 91/216.

question: Paige is laying square pavers for a backyard patio. The patio will be a rectangle 20 feet by 16 feet, and each paver is 24 inches on a side. The pavers fit exactly, with no cutting. How many pavers does Paige need?
explanation: 1. 24 inches is 2 feet. Along the length: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 pavers. 2. Along the width: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 pavers. 3. Total: 10 × 8 = 80 pavers.

question: A muffin recipe makes 12 muffins and uses 1/4 cup of sugar. Elena needs 36 muffins for a school bake sale. The muffins bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes. If she scales the recipe exactly, how many cups of sugar will she need?
explanation: 1. Scale factor: 36 ÷ 12 = 3. 2. Sugar: 1/4 × 3 = 3/4 cup.

question: Sam took his family out for brunch at a diner that opened 12 years ago. They ordered five pancake plates at $10 each and a pitcher of orange juice for $6. Sales tax is 6%, and they added a 15% tip figured on the food cost before tax. What was the total cost of the brunch, including tax and tip?
Theo's soccer team kept track of how many goals it scored in each game this season, shown in the table. Each game lasted 80 minutes. What is the median number of goals the team scored per game?
table: Goals scored | Number of games / 0 | 5 / 1 | 3 / 2 | 2 / 3 | 4 / 4 | 6 / 5 | 3
explanation: 1. Total: 5 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 3 = 23 games. 2. With 23 values in order, the median is the 12th value. 3. Running totals: through 0: 5, through 1: 8, through 2: 10, through 3: 14, through 4: 20, through 5: 23. 4. The 12th value falls in the row for 3 goals, so the median is 3 goals.

question: Ben keeps a tin of cookies on his desk. It holds 7 chocolate chip cookies and 5 oatmeal cookies, all the same size. The tin was a gift from his neighbor 4 years ago. Without looking, he takes out two cookies, one after the other, and doesn't put either back. What is the probability, as a fraction, that both cookies are the same kind?
explanation: 1. There are 7 + 5 = 12 cookies in all. 2. P(both chocolate chip) = 7/12 × 6/11 = 42/132. 3. P(both oatmeal) = 5/12 × 4/11 = 20/132. 4. Add the two cases: 42/132 + 20/132 = 62/132 = 31/66.

question: Arjun is laying a 3-by-8 patio of square tiles, all the same size. Looking at the grid lines, Arjun wonders how many squares can be traced, counting every size, from single tiles up to the biggest square that fits. How many squares of all sizes are in the 3-by-8 grid?
explanation: 1. A k-by-k square can start in 8 − k + 1 spots across and 3 − k + 1 spots down. 2. By size: 1-by-1: 24, 2-by-2: 14, 3-by-3: 6. 3. Total: 24 + 14 + 6 = 44.

question: Omar spends a rainy Saturday watching a baking show. He watches five episodes, and each one is 30 minutes long. How many hours of the show does Omar watch?
explanation: 1. Total: 5 × 30 = 150 minutes. 2. There are 60 minutes in an hour: 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours.

question: Marcus must be at work by 9:30 a.m. for a meeting. He walks 15 minutes to the train station, rides the train for 35 minutes, and then walks 10 minutes to the office. A train ticket costs $2.75, and a train leaves the moment he reaches the platform. It is 7:45 a.m. now. At most, how many minutes can Marcus wait before leaving home?
explanation: 1. Time needed: 15 + 35 + 10 = 60 minutes. 2. From 7:45 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. is 105 minutes. 3. Marcus can wait 105 − 60 = 45 minutes.

question: Ezra wants to buy a couch at a furniture store. The price is $903 if he pays all at once. The store also offers a payment plan: $200 down, then 12 monthly payments of $74. The couch is 84 inches long. How much more would Ezra pay in total with the payment plan than by paying all at once?
explanation: 1. Monthly payments: 12 × $74 = $888. 2. Payment plan total: $200 + $888 = $1,088. 3. Extra cost: $1,088 − $903 = $185.

question: Paige leans a 25-foot ladder against the side of her house to clean the gutters. For safety, the bottom of the ladder sits 7 feet out from the wall, on level ground. The ladder is rated to hold 300 pounds. How high up the wall does the top of the ladder reach, in feet?
explanation: 1. The wall, the ground and the ladder form a right triangle, with the ladder as the hypotenuse. 2. height² = 25² − 7² = 625 − 49 = 576. 3. height = √576 = 24 feet.

question: Felix is saving for a new bike. He puts $18 in a jar the first week, and every week after that he puts in $3 more than the week before. He started the plan on his 14th birthday. How much will Felix have saved in all after 19 weeks?
explanation: 1. Week 19: $18 + 18 × $3 = $72. 2. Pair week 1 with week 19, week 2 with week 18, and so on: each pair adds to $18 + $72 = $90. 3. With 19 weeks, the average week is $90 ÷ 2 = $45, so the total is 19 × $45 = $855.

question: Ingrid left home at 7:25 a.m. to drive to a lake cabin. She made no stops, and the dashboard clock read 10:35 a.m. when she pulled into the cabin's driveway. How many minutes did the drive take?
explanation: 1. From 7:25 a.m. to 8:00 a.m. is 35 minutes. 2. From 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m. is 2 hours, or 120 minutes. 3. From 10:00 a.m. to 10:35 a.m. is 35 minutes. 4. Total: 35 + 120 + 35 = 190 minutes.

question: Andre is driving 275 miles to a lake house, where he'll catch a ride home with family. His car gets 25 miles per gallon, and gas costs $4.20 per gallon. His car's tank holds 16 gallons. How much will gas cost for the drive?

Malik's world history grade is a weighted average of four categories. The table shows each category's weight and his average so far. There are 23 students in the class, and only the final exam is left. What score does Malik need on the final exam to finish with exactly a 90?
table: Category | Weight | Average / Homework | 20% | 98 / Quizzes | 20% | 82 / Midterm | 30% | 88 / Final exam | 30% | ?
explanation: 1. Points earned so far: 19.6 + 16.4 + 26.4 = 62.4. 2. To finish at 90, the final must add 90 − 62.4 = 27.6 points. 3. The final is worth 30%, so the score needed is 27.6 ÷ 0.3 = 92.

question: Algae is spreading across the pond on Priya's farm. Right now it covers 25 square feet, and the area it covers doubles every 3 days. The pond is about 5 feet deep. If it keeps doubling at this rate, how many square feet will the algae cover 15 days from now?
explanation: 1. 15 days ÷ 3 days = 5 doublings. 2. Double five times: 25 → 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 square feet.

question: A community center asked 50 members which summer trips they would sign up for. The results are in the table. The "Hiking trip" and "Kayaking trip" counts include the members who signed up for both trips. The sign-up sheet was posted for 18 days. How many members signed up for both trips?
table: Answer | Number of members / Hiking trip | 9 / Kayaking trip | 10 / Neither trip | 34
explanation: 1. At least one: 50 − 34 = 16. 2. Adding 9 + 10 = 19 counts the 'both' group twice. 3. So the extra count is the 'both' group: 19 − 16 = 3.

question: Today is Saturday. Amara's new gym pass starts tomorrow and is good for 80 days in a row. Her favorite spin class meets once a week, every Wednesday. How many Wednesday spin classes fall within the 80 days of her pass?
explanation: 1. 80 days = 11 full weeks (11 × 7 = 77) + 3 extra days. 2. Each full week has exactly one Wednesday: 11. 3. The 3 extra days fall on the same weekdays as the first 3: Sunday through Tuesday, which does not include a Wednesday. 4. Total: 11 + 0 = 11.

question: Mateo is saving for a pair of concert tickets that costs $145. He already has $45 saved and puts away $25 each week. How many more weeks will it take Mateo to have exactly enough?
explanation: 1. Still needed: $145 − $45 = $100. 2. $100 ÷ $25 per week = 4 weeks.

question: Lena bowls in a league with 22 teams. So far this season she has bowled three games, scoring 147, 129, and 123. She wants her average after the next game to be exactly 140. What score does Lena need in the next game?
explanation: 1. An average of 140 over 4 games means a total of 140 × 4 = 560. 2. Total so far: 147 + 129 + 123 = 399. 3. Needed: 560 − 399 = 161.

question: Maya is painting the four walls of her bedroom, which is 16 feet long, 13 feet wide and 8 feet high. She wants two coats on every wall. One gallon of paint covers 350 square feet with one coat, and the paint costs $45 a gallon. If paint is sold only in whole gallons, how many gallons does Maya need to buy?
explanation: 1. Wall area: 2 × (16 + 13) × 8 = 464 square feet. 2. Two coats: 464 × 2 = 928 square feet. 3. 928 ÷ 350 ≈ 2.7, which is more than 2, so round up to 3 gallons.

question: Theo is making trail mix for a weekend hike. His recipe mixes peanuts, raisins and chocolate chips in the ratio 3:6:1 by weight. He wants 40 ounces of trail mix in all, which he'll pack into four bags. How many ounces of peanuts should Theo use?
explanation: 1. Total parts: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10. 2. Each part is 40 ÷ 10 = 4 ounces. 3. Peanuts: 3 parts × 4 = 12 ounces.

question: Owen owns 8 shares of a company's stock. On Monday the share price rose 25%. On Tuesday it fell 40% from Monday's closing price. By what percent is Tuesday's closing price lower than the price before Monday's change?
explanation: 1. Start with a price of 100 (any starting value works the same way). 2. Up 25%: 100 → 125. 3. Then down 40%: 40% of 125 is 50, so 125 → 75. 4. 75 is 25 below 100, so it is 25% lower.

question: Paige wants to start going to a climbing gym and is choosing between the two plans in the table. The gym is open until 11 o'clock on weeknights. For how many visits would the two plans cost exactly the same?
table: Plan | One-time fee | Cost per visit / Member plan | $40 | $11 / Basic plan | $0 | $16
explanation: 1. Member plan costs $40 more up front. 2. Basic plan costs $5 more per visit, so each visit closes the gap by $5. 3. The gap closes after $40 ÷ $5 = 8 visits. 4. Check: $40 + 8 × $11 = $128 and $0 + 8 × $16 = $128, so the answer is 8 visits.

question: At an ice cream stand, customers build a sundae by choosing exactly 3 different toppings from a list of 9. Every sundae also gets one of 3 ice cream flavors: vanilla, chocolate or strawberry. Each sundae comes in a 12-ounce cup. The order the toppings are chosen in doesn't matter. How many different sundaes can a customer build?
explanation: 1. Pick 3 of 9 toppings: 9 × 8 × 7 = 504 ordered picks, ÷ 6 (the 3 × 2 × 1 orders of the same three) = 84 sets. 2. Each set can go with any of the 3 ice cream flavors: 84 × 3 = 252 sundaes.

question: Mateo spots a rolling suitcase with a price tag of $65. A sign on the rack says the price will be 40% off at the register. What is the sale price of the rolling suitcase, before tax?

Hana bikes to work. She rides 3 miles on a bike path at a steady 15 miles per hour, then 5 miles through city streets at a steady 10 miles per hour. Her office is on the third floor. How many minutes does the whole trip take?
explanation: 1. First part: 3 ÷ 15 = 1/5 hour, which is 12 minutes. 2. Second part: 5 ÷ 10 = 1/2 hour, which is 30 minutes. 3. Total: 12 + 30 = 42 minutes.

question: Nico's grandmother gave him $3,000 for his 18th birthday. He put all of it in a certificate of deposit that pays 8% interest, compounded once a year, and left it alone. How much will the certificate of deposit be worth after 2 years?

Malik is ordering pizza for five friends. The pizzeria sells round pizzas in two sizes: a 14-inch small and a 16-inch large, where the size is the diameter. Both have the same crust and toppings. The large pizza has how many times the area of the small pizza?
explanation: 1. Radii: 7 and 8 inches. 2. Areas: π × 7² = 49π and π × 8² = 64π. 3. Ratio: 64π ÷ 49π = 64/49.

question: Rosa is eleven times as old as her granddaughter, Ruth. Every summer the two of them go fishing at a lake 9 miles from home. Exactly 2 years ago, Rosa was sixteen times as old as Ruth. How old is Rosa now, in years?
explanation: 1. Let Ruth's age now be x, so Rosa is 11x. 2. 2 years ago: 11x − 2 = 16(x − 2) = 16x − 32. 3. Move the x terms to one side: 5x = 32 − 2 = 30, so x = 6. 4. So Rosa is 11 × 6 = 66 years old now. Check: 2 years ago, 64 = 16 × 4.
